Chapter 1

Before I spend a rupee, I find out where the money is leaking.

1

Meta and Google audits

The same four problems show up in most accounts.

Every audit ends in a list of fixes, not a report that sits in a drive.

FoundNo funnel strategy

Budget stuck at one stage, with no plan for warm or returning shoppers.

→
FixedFull funnel

Top, middle and bottom of funnel, each with its own job and budget.

FoundNo customer segmentation

New visitors, cart abandoners and past buyers all treated the same.

→
FixedSegments by intent

Audiences split by how close each group is to buying.

FoundAudience overlap

Ad sets bidding against each other for the same people, pushing costs up.

→
FixedExclusions and consolidation

Each segment excluded from the others, fewer and stronger ad sets.

FoundOne message for everyone

The same creative shown to strangers and loyal customers.

→
FixedContent per segment

A different message for each segment, matched to where they are.

Meta audit

What I check

  • Campaign structure and funnel coverage
  • Audience overlap and exclusions
  • Pixel and Conversions API events
  • Creative fatigue and format mix
Google audit

What I check

  • Campaign and keyword structure
  • Search terms and negatives
  • Performance Max asset groups
  • Conversion tracking and Shopping feed

What improves after: a cleaner account, budget going to the people most likely to buy, and every segment seeing a message made for it.

Funnel strategy

Each stage has its own audience, campaign and content.

StageWhoCampaignsContent
TopNew prospects, broad audiencesAdvantage+ Shopping, reach, YouTube, TikTokUGC, brand story, new launches
MiddleVideo viewers, engagers, site visitorsRetargeting, Demand GenProduct benefits, reviews, styling videos
BottomCart and checkout abandonersCatalog retargeting, Search, Shopping, PMaxOffers, bundles, urgency
RetainPast buyersCustomer lists, email, SMS, pushNew arrivals, cross-sell, early access

Segmentation and overlap

Different content for each segment, and no segment bidding against another.

New prospectsBrand story and UGC that shows the product in real life
Engaged viewersReviews, product proof and styling ideas
Cart abandonersA reminder of what they left, plus a reason to finish
Past buyersNew arrivals and products that go with what they bought
Loyal customersEarly access and members-first offers

Every segment is excluded from the others, so ad sets don't compete for the same person and costs stay down.

Welcome flow

Four emails over five days for a skincare brand.

A 10% code, then problem, solution and proof, ending with an expiry reminder. Checkout subscribers are excluded, so the discount only goes to new prospects.

  1. Trigger

    Subscribes to email

    Only people who didn't subscribe at checkout.

  2. Day 0

    Here's your 10% off

    The code up front, with bestsellers.

  3. Day 2

    Match your skin concern

    Each problem paired with the product that solves it.

  4. Day 4

    Is this you?

    A diagnosis-style story that builds a routine.

  5. Day 5

    Your code is about to expire

    Urgency plus reviews to close the first order.

How a brand lands

The six steps behind every market plan.

  1. Know the audienceWho buys, where they shop and what they expect
  2. Position the brandWhat makes it right for this market
  3. Pick the channelsMeta, Google, TikTok, Snapchat, by market
  4. Plan the launchPre-launch, launch and post-launch
  5. Localize contentLanguage, seasons, sizing and culture
  6. Measure and adaptEarly signals decide where to scale
